title: Sicilian Defense: Smith-Morra Gambit
line: White gives a pawn for fast development; Black takes it, and a careless move by White meets a trap.

steps.text: Here White pushes the pawn on d2 two squares at once.
Take the pawn. It removes White's center pawn.
Take the second pawn too. White takes back once and is a pawn down, but gets quick development for it.
Bring the knight out. It watches d4 and e5.

also.e7e6: That also works. This lesson brings the knight out first.
also.d7d6: That also works. This lesson brings the knight out first.

steps.text: Push the pawn on e7 one square. It guards d5, so a white knight that jumps there can be taken.

also.d7d6: That is also played. This lesson goes on with the other pawn.

steps.text: Bring the queen to c7. She watches e5 and stands on a file with no pawns on it. This is the Siberian setup.

also.a7a6: That is the most played move here, and just as sound. This lesson follows the Siberian setup with the queen.

steps.text: Jump to g4 with the knight. With your queen it eyes h2, next to White's king.
steps.after: White slips here. Chasing the knight with this pawn is a mistake.

steps.text: Jump into d4 with the other knight. It hits White's queen and the knight that guards h2.
steps.after: If White's knight takes yours, your queen mates on h2. If White's queen steps away, your knight takes on f3 with check.

summary: Black takes the gambit pawns and develops. If White chases the knight carelessly, a second knight jump decides.
